text: HCM City's banking deposits and credit expand in first 10 months of 2026

Total deposits at credit institutions in Ho Chi Minh City reached over VND5.9 quadrillion ($224 billion) in the first ten months of 2026, up 12.2% from the end of 2025 and 17.52% year-on-year, according to the State Bank of Vietnam's Regional Branch 2.
The growth has helped ensure sufficient funding to meet credit demand, support businesses and drive economic expansion in the final months of the year.
Outstanding loans in the city totalled VND5.857 quadrillion in the first 10 months of 2026, up 12.5% from the end of last year and 18.2% year-on-year.

In its report, the State Bank of Vietnam's Regional Branch 2 described the figures as a positive signal for the local monetary market and banking sector, contributing to the effective implementation of monetary policy objectives in 2026.
Banking activity in Ho Chi Minh City is forecast to remain robust during the final two months of the year.
Total outstanding credit is projected to reach approximately VND5.85 quadrillion, equivalent to an increase of 12.4% from the end of 2025.
Lending is expected to remain focused on production, business activities and other sectors driving economic growth.

Notably, foreign-currency loans amounted to VND288 trillion, accounting for 4.9% of total outstanding credit and rising 42% from the end of last year, reflecting positive growth in import-export activities.
